claims.text: Run the secret floor before anything leaves the process.
claims.why: Function is called before subprocess spawning in this module's flow; no evidence of other calls but within this chunk it is the only floor invocation.

claims.text: sensitivity.secret_floor_rule has two INDEPENDENT channels: path markers checked against path, value-shaped regexes checked against text.
claims.why: The implementation calls secret_floor_rule with (path, "") and (path, text), but the internal behavior of secret_floor_rule is not in this chunk.

claims.text: A council prompt is question + evidence + a multi-file diff, so there is no single path.
claims.why: The prompt construction is not in this chunk; only the floor_check function is visible.

claims.text: the tempting secret_floor_rule("", prompt) kills the path tier outright: a patch that ADDS .env or config/id_rsa sails through, because the only trace of the filename is diff --git a/.env b/.env inside text, which no content regex matches.
claims.why: The behavior of secret_floor_rule and the regex patterns are not in this chunk; the claim about what the floor rule matches cannot be verified.

claims.text: So the channels are driven separately and PER FILE, exactly as the floor's own docstring requires:
claims.why: The code iterates evidence_paths individually and evidence_files as (path, text) pairs, calling secret_floor_rule per item.

claims.text: evidence_paths -- every changed path (PatchArtifact.changed_paths) and every evidence file path, each through the PATH channel alone;
claims.why: The caller's argument construction (PatchArtifact) is not in this chunk; the function does call secret_floor_rule(path, "") for each path.

claims.text: evidence_files -- (path, text) pairs, both channels, per file;
claims.why: The function calls secret_floor_rule(path, text or "") for each pair, which uses both path and text.

claims.text: prompt -- a content-channel BACKSTOP for a credential pasted into the question itself. It is a backstop, never the whole check.
claims.why: The prompt is checked last and only if no earlier refusal; it is called with empty path and the prompt text.

claims.text: Returns the first FloorRefusal, or None.
claims.why: Each rule hit returns immediately; if no rule hits, returns None.

claims.text: A hit means REFUSE -- there is no redact-and-send.
claims.why: Function returns the FloorRefusal without any redaction or alternative.

claims.text: Tier-2 allow-list result for an untrusted participant, per path.
claims.why: Function returns tuple of paths where slice_egress_rule returns true for untrusted lanes.

claims.text: Not a decision made by a default argument: an untrusted lane means OpenAI / Google get the allow-list
claims.why: The mapping of lane to specific vendors is not in this chunk; only the lane check is visible.

claims.text: and every withheld path is named on the reply so a reader can see what the council did NOT see.
claims.why: The reply construction is not in this chunk; only the computation of withheld paths is visible.

claims.text: Environment for a council subprocess, with OLLAMA_HOST STRIPPED.
claims.why: Function copies os.environ and pops OLLAMA_HOST unconditionally.

claims.text: Never set, never mutated, never inherited -- see the module docstring.
claims.why: The module docstring is not in this chunk; the function only strips OLLAMA_HOST, does not set or mutate the input.

claims.text: A council that normalises a remote Ollama into a shared environment silently invalidates offload.py's trusted-lane justification repo-wide.
claims.why: offload.py is not in this chunk; the function's effect on that file cannot be verified.

claims.text: A fresh, EMPTY temp directory to spawn a council subprocess in.
claims.why: Function creates a TemporaryDirectory with prefix 'dcouncil-cwd-' which is empty and fresh per call.

claims.text: Not the repo, not a worktree, containing no repo files.
claims.why: The temp directory is created by tempfile.TemporaryDirectory, not from repo; no repo files are copied in.

claims.text: Returned as a context manager so the directory is fresh per call and removed after.
claims.why: Returns a TemporaryDirectory object which is a context manager and cleans up after exit.

claims.text: Raises if the system temp dir somehow sits under repo_root, because a reviewer rooted in the checkout is the failure this exists to prevent.
claims.why: Function checks if root is in here.parents and raises ValueError with cleanup.

claims.text: Default runner: spawn argv under spine.cancel.ManagedProcess.
claims.why: Function uses ManagedProcess with argv, cwd, env.

claims.text: THE PROMPT IS NEVER IN argv.
claims.why: argv is passed through; the prompt is written to in_path and given as stdin, not in argv.

claims.text: It is staged to a temp file and handed over as the child's stdin.
claims.why: Function writes stdin_text to in_path and opens it as fin, passed as stdin.

claims.text: A file rather than a pipe because a CLI that never drains stdin deadlocks the writer OUTSIDE every timeout
claims.why: The claim about deadlock behavior is not observable in this chunk; the code uses a file, which is consistent.

claims.text: and because on the ssh path a command-line prompt is re-parsed by the remote login shell, which turns any backtick or $(...) in a diff into remote code execution with no adversarial model required.
claims.why: The ssh path is not in this chunk; the function just uses stdin file.

claims.text: The whole process TREE dies on timeout.
claims.why: The function calls proc.cancel() when timeout, but the behavior of cancel (whether it kills the whole tree) is in ManagedProcess, not in this chunk.

claims.text: Popen.terminate reaches the immediate child only; a hung vendor's grandchildren outlive it.
claims.why: This is a claim about Popen.terminate; the code uses ManagedProcess.cancel, not Popen. The behavior of Popen is not in this chunk.

claims.text: Fail closed: a child we could not contain must never be left running.
claims.why: On CancellationUnavailable or OSError, the function returns a RunResult with spawn_error, not leaving any process (since ManagedProcess context manager would have cleaned up).

claims.text: A read-only, tool-less, one-shot invocation of a vendor CLI.
claims.why: The profile definitions show tool denial flags, but the actual CLI behavior is not in this chunk.

claims.text: args never contains the prompt: stdin_prompt is always true here and the shape is enforced by test, not by convention.
claims.why: The test enforcement is not in this chunk; the profiles defined here show stdin_prompt=True and args do not contain prompt, but the claim about tests cannot be verified.

claims.text: Forbidden anywhere in a council argv. workspace-write and dontAsk are the two flags that turn a reviewer into an agent with an editor.
claims.why: The tuple contains 'workspace-write' and 'dontAsk' among others, and _assert_profile_safe checks for them.

claims.text: Tools are named explicitly rather than allow-listing nothing: the variadic --allowed-tools <tools...> would swallow the next flag if given an empty value, so the denial is expressed with the = form, which cannot slurp.
claims.why: The profile uses '--disallowed-tools=...' form with explicit list, not '--allowed-tools'.

claims.text: read-only sandbox + approvals never; --skip-git-repo-check because the council cwd is a bare temp dir by design and codex otherwise refuses.
claims.why: The openai profile includes '--sandbox', 'read-only', '--ask-for-approval', 'never', and '--skip-git-repo-check'.

claims.text: Common shape. Subclasses implement _dispatch only.
claims.why: The class body is cut off; only the docstring and initial attributes are visible.

claims.text: ask is the ONLY entry point, and it always: charges the token ceiling, runs the secret floor, computes withheld paths for an untrusted lane, times the call, and maps every failure onto STATUSES.
claims.why: The ask method is not in this chunk; only the class declaration and docstring are visible.

claims.text: A refusal is a STATUS, not an exception -- a council must never lose a participant to a traceback, because a missing turn is indistinguishable from a turn that was never sought.
claims.why: The failure mapping is not in this chunk.

observations.what: council_cwd checks if repo_root is a parent of the temp dir, but not if repo_root is a child of the temp dir; the docstring says 'system temp dir somehow sits under repo_root', which is exactly what is checked, so no issue.
run_managed catches FileNotFoundError and (CancellationUnavailable, OSError) separately; the first returns spawn_error 'not_on_path', the second 'spawn_failed'. Both are fail-closed.
The timeout loop polls every 0.02 seconds; if timeout_s is 0, deadline is started, so it may immediately cancel after first poll, which is fine.

The floor_check returns FloorRefusal with channel 'path' for path-only hits, and for evidence_files it determines channel by rule.startswith('secret path marker') else 'content'. This matches the docstring's two-channel model.
The COUNCIL_PROFILES are validated at module load via _assert_profile_safe, which checks only the command and args strings; this is a static check that cannot catch runtime flag parsing issues.
